header.policy: POTENTIAL_OUTCOME_BYPASS findings can never be closed via OUT_OF_SCOPE; both were closed with real code changes and regression tests.

integrated: OutcomeService consumes the approved verification plan (digest-bound); callers can never override verification inputs

closures.title: BrokerExecutionResult deserialization as a receipt ingestion path
closures.call_path: any future serde_json::from_str::<BrokerExecutionResult>(caller JSON) or generic DeserializeOwned bound over the type
closures.external_reachability: none today (no production deserialization call site exists - verified by grep); the risk was latent capability
closures.risk: a caller-shaped { success: true, exit_code: 0, plan_id: ... } JSON could be deserialized into a receipt-looking value and treated as execution authority by future code
closures.fix: removed the Deserialize derive from BrokerExecutionResult. The type is Serialize-only; any attempt to deserialize it fails at COMPILE TIME in every cargo check/clippy/test build. The doc comment freezes the rationale and forbids re-adding the derive without a CP-level security review.
closures.tests: compile-time enforcement (no runtime test possible by design: the negative property is that compilation fails); the existing receipt authority tests (receipt_store_is_the_only_execution_authority) keep asserting the runtime boundary
closures.final_disposition: CLOSED - compile-time, no runtime bypass possible

closures.title: recordDecisionOutcome free-text journal read as verified execution outcomes
closures.call_path: MCP dispatch (dispatch.ts:2214) -> decision journal metadata.outcomes + event entity; risk was any future consumer promoting these records into CP8 verified outcomes
closures.external_reachability: MCP tool surface (decision outcome recording); the journal itself is a legitimate product feature
closures.risk: caller/LLM-authored free-text actual_outcome could be silently read as a verified outcome by future code, creating a parallel outcome authority
closures.fix: every journaled record is now stamped with machine-readable markers outcome_authority: 'journal' and verified: false (both in the decision metadata outcomes array and on the outcome event entity). The outcome layer has no import of decision-store (structurally asserted in goal24-outcome-hardening.test.ts) and consumes only trusted receipt/observation ids.
closures.tests: goal24-outcome-hardening.test.ts: (a) journaled records carry outcome_authority=journal + verified=false at both storage sites; (b) no brain-server/src/outcome/** file imports decision-store
closures.final_disposition: CLOSED - journal is typed non-authoritative and structurally unreachable from the outcome layer

closure_method_policy: Neither potential was closed via OUT_OF_SCOPE. Both were closed with real code changes (derive removal + typed journal markers) and automated regression tests. blocks_before = 0 and blocks_after = 0: nothing blocked CP8 and nothing remains blocking.
